what: The battle mix: how every approved battle sound is blended by unit, distance and how hot the fight is, so a battle plays like a war film. Numbers are the sound director's to tune; the 3D game reads them. Spec in plain words: battle-mix.md beside this file.
changes: v2 (18 Nov 16:00Z): impacts, to match the art director's explosion sheet; grenades and bomb sticks added to big; air: passByPlane, gunsByPlane, one pass per group, no ricochets in the air, formation drone +1.5 dB; beds.place (wind, woods, rain: approved 18 Nov); campaign map hammer real; loops bus -6 dB; air gunsByCalibre, engineLost, windmilling, distance air_guns; voices lifted only as the fight thickens; explosions full to 30 m, not 60, so a shell at 25 m lands about 6 dB harder than one at 80 m (the 84 s preview was made with v1).
units: metres of the battlefield (the sims' x, y), seconds, decibels. 0 dB = the file as made.

listener.at: the ground point the camera looks at, raised by heightFactor x the camera's height above it
listener.facing: the camera's yaw, so left on screen is heard on the left

bed.note: layer 1: the battle's air, near and far (beds crossfade by intensity)

loops.note: layer 2: engines, marching, a unit's own fight loop. v2: -6, so an engine ticking over beside the listener sits about 10 dB under a shot at the same distance (at 0 it was level with the blasts when the camera looked at a tank)

close.note: layer 3: shots, bursts, impacts, footsteps, falls, placed at the unit

voices.note: layer 4: orders and cries, one per side at once, never cut off; while a line speaks the close layer dips 4 dB, as a film keeps its words clear. v2: lifted to gainDb only as the fight thickens (calmGainDb below the meter's 0.3, gainDb from 0.5): in a lull a shout at +6 was as loud as a shell landing at 25 m

big.note: layer 5: big moments, always play, duck the rest

music.note: the player's music setting still scales this

master.note: a limiter on the whole battle so stacked blasts never clip

distance._how: full = no loss up to here; past it the level falls rolloff x the inverse-distance law (4.5 dB a doubling), tapering to nothing over the last 40% before silent. lpf = [distance, low-pass Hz] points: far sounds lose their top, as in air. reverb = [distance, send 0..1]: far sounds are wetter. farTakesFrom: beyond this play the family's far takes instead of the close ones, at the level the close take would have had (add closeLUFS - farLUFS from sound-list.json: the pack's far takes are already quieter).

mg.note: an MG 42 at 300 m is still its own rip: far takes only past 500 m

body.note: footsteps, kit, knees, falls: heard only zoomed in

air_guns.note: guns fired in the air: no echo (nothing to echo from) and no far takes (the pack's far bursts are heard across ground); past about 1.5 km the engines bury them

flashToBang._how: Sound travels at 343 m/s: a gun or blast farther than `from` is heard after its flash, by distance / 343 s, never more than maxSeconds, divided by the battle clock's speed (x4 before contact).

places._how: The reverb a sound is sent to, by the ground under the unit making it (cover). Return level 1.0 (send x 1.0 comes back at the same energy).

open.note: long, thin tail: the fight rolling off over fields

buildings.note: hard echo off walls: why a town fight sounds closer and harsher

intensity._how: How hot the fight is round the listener, 0 to 1, worked out every 0.25 s. heat = sum over shots and blasts heard in the last `window` seconds of weight x closeness (1 at the listener, 0 at `radius`), plus perBlockFighting for each block in act 'fight' within blockRadius. target = min(1, heat / fullAt). The meter rises toward target with time constant `rise` and falls with `fall` (a fight calms slowly, as in a film).
intensity.zoomedOut: above 400 m camera height also blend in the share of all blocks fighting anywhere (0..1), weight 0.5, so a wide view of a big battle still roars

beds._how: Layer 1. Each bed's gain follows intensity: silent below `in`, full (gainDb) from `full` to `hold`, gone above `out`. Equal-power crossfades, never faster than 2 s. Not placed: they surround the listener (spread 100%).

list.name: rifles_far_loop
list.note: a fight somewhere off in the distance

beds.beforeContact: until the first contact only rifles_far_loop at -14 dB plays, after the battle's first few seconds; and a far salvo (far_guns_01..03) 2 to 2.6 km off every 15 to 30 s: the war somewhere else

place._how: Under the battle beds: the air of the place itself (approved by Brian 18 Nov 15:52Z). Not placed (spread 100%). Picked by the ground round the listener; crossfaded over `crossfade` s when it changes. Loudest before contact, sinking toward atFullDb as the meter climbs, because a war film lets the wind be heard only in the lulls.

rain._note: rain plays on top of the place's bed, and stays heard through the fight

variety._how: Every one-shot gets a small random pitch and level so no shot is a copy of the last, and never the same take twice running.

limits._how: At most this many of a family at once; when full, the farthest and quietest is dropped first. Voices are never cut: a new line waits for the last to end.
limits.sameLoopShare: units on the same loop within 80 m of each other share one playing loop, placed at their middle, 1.5 dB louder per extra unit up to +4.5 dB

music._how: Battle music (mood 'battle': advance, trench_line) steps aside when the fighting is thick and comes back at the turning points, as a film score does. Levels are dB under the player's music setting; every change is a fade of `fade` seconds.

nearBreak.note: either side at three quarters: the swing of the battle

ownBroken.note: falls away; the defeat stinger follows

big._how: Layer 5: always plays, ducks the rest for a moment (attack, hold, release).
big._landings: for a shell, mortar bomb, grenade or bomb landing, impacts.bySize.bigWithin decides instead (the same 60 m for every shell)

impacts._how: A shell, mortar bomb, grenade or bomb landing. Matches the art director's explosion sheet (art-director/explosions/explosions-look.md, 'Inside it' item 4): the flash, then the bang; near hits a sharp crack, a deep thump and earth coming down; far hits a low rumble only; a shell within 60 m is a big moment. The band is the hit's distance from the listener. Flash then bang past 150 m comes from flashToBang, the level and air from distance.explosions.

near._sound: the crack and thump of a close take, then earth coming down (debris, below)

debris._how: earth and stones landing 0.9 to 3 s after a near hit, when the picture's clods land (thickest 1.5 to 2.5 s): the falling part of shell_impact_near_02 (2.3 to 4.9 s into it) starts `after` s after the flash, at the hit's level and place. Under shell_impact_near it is laid on top. shell_impact_near_02 itself plays only to cutAt (cutFade s fade) and its own falling part is moved up the same way. explosion_debris has its own earth in its first 2 s.
debris._db: lifted 12 dB over its natural level: at 0 the falling earth sat under the bed and an idling engine (measured on the 105 mm test clip), so it is brought up as film sound does

far._sound: a low rumble only: takes recorded far off (no crack left), heard distance / 343 s after the flash

incoming._how: the rush a shell makes in the last moment before it lands (the art sheet's -0.8 s). Played only where a real recording exists.
incoming._why: No real recording of a shell coming in has been found yet. The two found are the film convention's long falling whistle, not the sound of a shell, so the moment is the crack and the blast, as tank and anti-tank guns are on the sheet. bomb_release is a real falling bomb (approved).

bySize._how: db is added to the take's level, bigWithin is how near a landing counts as a big moment. Same recordings for every calibre (the pack has no per-calibre takes); a bigger shell is louder and heard farther. Bombs land as bomb_stick_01 when a stick falls.

salvo._how: a battery's shells never land in step (as the art sheet asks): 0.2 to 1.5 s apart, and never the same take twice running

shellShock._how: Rare. A blast within `within` metres of the listener while the camera is lower than `cameraBelow`: every world sound (not music, not the desk) goes dull for a moment, as if your ears were hit. No ringing tone: nothing made up.

fireModel._how: The sims fight blocks against blocks with no single shots, so the screen makes the shots: a block in act 'fight' fires these, timed here. Rates are per block; wavering x0.6, routing stops firing. Close takes inside the family's farTakesFrom, far takes beyond.

impact.at: the engaged block, or the zone it shells

incoming._how: an enemy block firing on a block within `within` of the listener: the crack of rounds going past

rifle._note: the real Mauser stands in for every bolt rifle without its own recording; the American takes garand_clip_ping after every 8th shot, then garand_reload

orders._note: no real Italian, French, Polish or Japanese voices yet: those armies are silent rather than given someone else's language

loops._how: What a unit plays while it does what it does (replaces the 'loop' names in src/battle/core/cues.ts, which still carry names of the rejected made-up set).
loops._fightNote: a block in a fight keeps its engine loop but carries no fight loop of its own: the fight is its shots (fireModel) plus the shared beds. That is what lets near and far blend instead of every block playing the same battle_loop.

contact.then: one order from the attacker's nation

rename._how: Names still in the battle code that are not real sounds (they belonged to the rejected made-up set, or Brian cut them). Left side: the name in the code. Right side: what to play, or null for silence.

campaign map (CampaignSounds.cpp)._note: hammer: a real anvil, approved 18 Nov 15:51Z. horses and ship_horn: Brian cut two rounds of takes, so silent

loops._how: each formation's own engines, by its model
loops._note: fourEngined (Lancaster, Halifax, Pe-8 and the rest): no recording of their own, the formation drone; twinEngined (He 111, Ju 88, Do 17, Wellington, B-25, SM.79): the B-25's engines

flak._how: inside the flak ring: a gun fires every `every` seconds, its shell bursts `burstAfter` later at the bombers' height
flak._soundEvery: bursts closer than this are not all heard: only the nearest plays (the picture keeps them all)

air.bedsByIntensity: same beds idea: aero_engine_idle_loop far off when quiet; the formation loops (b17_drone_loop, b24_drone_loop, bomber_heavy_loop, bomber_medium_loop) on each bomber group; fighter_engine_loop on fighters
air.passes: a fighter group passing within 300 m of the listener plays ONE pass take for the group, the nearest plane's, +1.5 dB, Doppler on: the same recording laid on itself a few hundredths of a second apart combs and sounds processed

passByPlane._why: no Bf 109 recording: the Spitfire's single V12 is the nearest real engine to its Daimler-Benz V12; fighter_pass is a twin-engined P-38 and B-25 sped up, for planes with nothing nearer

air.guns: dogfight / plane_guns / gunner_burst as the groups fight, distance family aircraft

gunsByPlane._why: the short form. Where the air battle sends each gun kind's firing, gunsByCalibre wins: a Bf 109 is then its machine guns plus the cannon. (Corrected 18 Nov 21:00Z: the pack does have a cannon, flak_light_fire's burst; see gunsByCalibre.)

gunsByCalibre._how: What plays while a gun kind fires in the air (the air battle sends each fighter group's rate of fire, each turret firing). Bursts are laid end to end while it fires, family air_guns, the same take never under 0.15 s after itself. `part` plays only that stretch of a take, faded over fadeOut at its end: the rest is the ground's echo, which the sky does not have.

rifle.wingOfFourOrMore: both takes together, the second 30 ms later
rifle._what: MG 17, .303 Browning, 7.7 mm, MG 15, MG 81: a real MG 42, whose 1,200 rounds a minute is their rate (its uploader added a few layers)

heavy._what: .50 Browning, 12.7 mm, MG 131, Berezin: real heavy machine guns

cannon._what: MG FF, MG 151/20, Hispano, ShVAK, the Zero's Type 99: a real 35 mm anti-aircraft cannon's burst, six rounds at about 600 a minute (the 20 mm guns' rate), without the roll after it. Heavier than a 20 mm; the nearest real cannon in the pack

handHeldRifle._what: a single hand-held rifle-calibre gun (MG 15, MG 81, Vickers K): one take at a time

engineLost.drone: the bomber's own drone drops by 10 x log10(engines left / engines): -1.2 dB on three of four, -3 dB on two of four, -3 dB on one of two
engineLost._why: no real recording of an aero engine cutting out or coughing: silent apart from the drone dropping

windmilling._why: no real recording of a windmilling propeller: silent

air._sameTakeGap: two of the same take never start less than 0.15 s apart (later one waits or drops): closer, they comb

roundsPassing._why: in the air there is no ground for rounds to glance off, so no ricochets (bullets_incoming_*); rounds passing the listener crack. No real recording of rounds striking a plane yet

air._groupLoopDb: a formation's engines within 80 m share one loop at +1.5 dB whatever the count: the drone is the bed under the guns, not over them
air.noBedNoEcho: at the bombers' height there is nothing to echo from: no reverb send, no ground bed

sea.note: ships' guns and blasts roll across water: place 'water' reverb on everything at sea
